q1: SELECT b1.name AS bar1, b2.name AS bar2 FROM bar AS b1, bar AS b2 WHERE NOT EXISTS(SELECT s1.beer FROM serves AS s1 WHERE s1.bar = b1.name AND NOT EXISTS(SELECT 1 FROM serves AS s2 WHERE s2.bar = b2.name AND s2.beer = s1.beer)) AND EXISTS(SELECT s2.beer FROM serves AS s2 WHERE s2.bar = b2.name AND NOT EXISTS(SELECT 1 FROM serves AS s1 WHERE s1.bar = b1.name AND s1.beer = s2.beer))
q2: SELECT DISTINCT S1.bar, S2.bar FROM serves AS S1 LEFT JOIN serves AS S2 ON S1.beer = S2.beer
q1_prompt_sql: SELECT b1.name AS bar1, b2.name AS bar2 FROM bar AS b1, bar AS b2 WHERE NOT EXISTS(SELECT s1.beer FROM serves AS s1 WHERE s1.bar = b1.name AND NOT EXISTS(SELECT 1 FROM serves AS s2 WHERE s2.bar = b2.name AND s2.beer = s1.beer)) AND EXISTS(SELECT s2.beer FROM serves AS s2 WHERE s2.bar = b2.name AND NOT EXISTS(SELECT 1 FROM serves AS s1 WHERE s1.bar = b1.name AND s1.beer = s2.beer))
q2_prompt_sql: SELECT DISTINCT S1.bar, S2.bar FROM serves AS S1 LEFT JOIN serves AS S2 ON S1.beer = S2.beer
counterexample: INSERT INTO Bar (name, address) VALUES ('BarA', 'AddressA'), ('BarB', 'AddressB'), ('BarC', 'AddressC'); INSERT INTO Beer (name, brewer) VALUES ('BeerX', 'BrewerX'), ('BeerY', 'BrewerY'); INSERT INTO Serves (bar, beer, price) VALUES ('BarA', 'BeerX', 10.00), ('BarA', 'BeerY', 12.00), ('BarB', 'BeerX', 10.00), ('BarC', 'BeerY', 12.00);
explanation: Q1 and Q2 are not equivalent. Q1 checks for bars that serve all beers served by another bar and at least one beer that no other bar serves. Q2 lists all pairs of bars that serve the same beer.
counterexample_dsp: Q1 will not return any results if no bar serves all beers served by another bar. Q2 will return all pairs of bars that serve the same beer.
